subject: forensic-medicine
title: Sulphuric Acid, Vitriolage and Nitric Acid

steps.title: Sulphuric acid, oil of vitriol
steps.tx: **Sulphuric acid**, oil of vitriol, is a heavy, odourless, colourless, non fuming, hygroscopic oily liquid that carbonises organic material; the commercial acid is brown or dark. It burns skin superficially after one second of contact and through its full thickness after thirty seconds. Inside the body it corrodes mouth, throat and oesophagus on contact, which is why five to ten millilitres can kill within twelve to twenty four hours.
steps.say: Oil of vitriol chars what it touches in seconds, and five to ten millilitres swallowed can kill within a day.

steps.title: Signs of swallowed sulphuric acid
steps.tx: The **signs of sulphuric acid poisoning** begin at the lips: swollen excoriated lips with brown or black streaks running from the mouth angles down the chin and neck where acid flowed. There is immediate burning pain, corrosion of mouth and throat, stridor, drooling and painful difficult swallowing, then epigastric pain spreading over abdomen and thorax. The vomit is brown or black, mucoid, strongly acid and may carry shreds of charred stomach wall, with intense thirst that provokes vomiting when satisfied.
steps.say: Black streaks from the mouth angles, charred shreds in brown vomit and thirst that reprovokes vomiting announce sulphuric acid.

steps.tx: The **signs of sulphuric acid poisoning** start at the mouth. Lips swell and excoriate, and brown or black streaks run from the angles down the chin and neck along the flow. Burning pain, corrosion of mouth and throat, stridor, drooling, and painful swallowing follow, then epigastric pain spreading over the abdomen and chest. Vomit is brown or black, mucoid, strongly acid, and may hold shreds of charred stomach wall. Intense thirst makes the patient drink, and drinking brings the vomit back.
steps.say: Swollen lips with black streaks down the chin, stridor, drooling, and pain on swallowing begin sulphuric acid injury. Brown black acid vomit may contain charred shreds of stomach, and thirst only restarts the vomiting.

steps.title: Local findings: teeth, tongue and abdomen
steps.tx: Inside the mouth the **teeth turn chalky white** and the tongue swells, sodden and black. The abdomen distends and becomes very tender, constipation is severe with tenesmus, the voice turns hoarse and husky from laryngeal injury, eyes sink and pupils usually dilate while the mind stays clear until death. That preserved clarity amid agony is repeatedly described in corrosive poisoning and helps separate it from narcotic or alcoholic collapse at the bedside.
steps.say: Chalky teeth, a black sodden tongue, a rigid tender abdomen and a clear mind form the bedside portrait of acid poisoning.

steps.title: Treatment: dilute, never lavage
steps.tx: **Treatment of sulphuric acid poisoning** forbids gastric lavage and emetics absolutely. Within thirty minutes the acid is diluted and neutralised in place with a quarter litre of water, milk, milk of magnesia, lime water, soap suds or aluminium hydroxide gel. Carbonates and bicarbonates are banned because liberated carbon dioxide distends and may rupture the stomach. Demulcents such as olive oil, milk and egg white follow, prednisolone sixty milligrams daily is given against stricture and shock, and tracheostomy answers glottis oedema.
steps.say: Dilute with milk or magnesia in the first half hour, never lavage, never bicarbonate, and secure the airway before anything else.

rows: Quarter litre water or milk early

steps.title: Postmortem picture of acid corrosion
steps.tx: At autopsy the **corrosion pattern of sulphuric acid** shows necrotic areas at lips, mouth, throat, chin and hands, greyish white at first then brown or black and leathery. Internally the injury hugs the upper digestive tract: squamous oesophagus is relatively resistant with superficial reaction, while the columnar stomach suffers coagulation eschar, sometimes converted wholly into a soft spongy black mass that disintegrates at touch, with perforation into the peritoneum and chemical peritonitis in survivors of hours.
steps.say: The oesophagus resists while the stomach blackens into a spongy mass, and perforation spills chemical peritonitis into the abdomen.

steps.title: Time course and late strictures
steps.tx: Corrosive injury evolves through **four time stages**. The acute inflammatory stage runs four to seven days with perforation and acidosis risk. Granulation occupies the next phase to about a week. Perforation is commonest between seven and twenty one days, when the wall is weakest. Cicatrisation begins at three weeks and can continue for years, and its overproduced scar is what strangles the oesophagus and pylorus. A four centimetre mercury filled bougie passed daily treats an established oesophageal stricture.
steps.say: Perforation peaks in the weak second and third weeks, and the scar that follows can stricture the gullet for years.

steps.title: Circumstances of sulphuric acid poisoning
steps.tx: Most swallowed cases are suicidal under **circumstances of acid poisoning**. Homicidal use is rare because the acid taste, near immediate local action and visible changes in food betray it at the first sip. Accidents arise from mistaking acid for castor oil or from vapour inhalation in chemical factories. It is also taken or injected vaginally as an abortifacient, which the examiner remembers in criminal abortion deaths with corrosive injuries of the genital tract.
steps.say: Suicide swallows acid, homicide is betrayed by its taste, and factories and abortionists account for most of the rest.

steps.title: Vitriolage, acid thrown to disfigure
steps.tx: **Vitriolage** is throwing sulphuric acid, occasionally nitric or carbolic acid, alkali or marking nut and calotropis juice, on another person to disfigure and harm, typically from jealousy. The burns are described as painless at first yet penetrating, devitalising tissue and predisposing to infection, with slow repair and contracture of scar. Blindness follows eye involvement. Treatment is immediate washing with plenty of water and soap or carbonate, then magnesium oxide paste, with eyes irrigated and oiled.
steps.say: Thrown acid devitalises and blinds rather than kills, so flood with water at once and irrigate eyes for a quarter hour.

nodes.label: Flood skin with water and soap

steps.title: Nitric acid and the xanthoproteic reaction
steps.tx: **Nitric acid**, aqua fortis, is a clear colourless fuming heavy liquid with a choking odour that stains organic matter yellow by producing picric acid, the **xanthoproteic reaction**. Symptoms mirror sulphuric acid with more eructation and abdominal distension from gas, yellow discolouration of tissues including the crowns of the teeth, and yellow stains on clothing that identify the acid at the scene. Inhaled fumes injure the respiratory tract directly, adding a pulmonary route to the corrosive gut injury.
steps.say: Yellow skin, yellow tooth crowns and yellow cloth stains are nitric acid signing its work through the xanthoproteic reaction.

steps.tx: **Nitric acid**, also called aqua fortis, is a clear colourless fuming heavy liquid with a choking smell. It stains organic matter yellow by forming picric acid, the xanthoproteic reaction. The illness resembles sulphuric acid but with more belching and abdominal distension from gas, yellow tissues including the tooth crowns, and yellow marks on clothing that name the acid at the scene. Inhaled fumes also burn the airway, adding lung injury to the corroded gut.
steps.say: Nitric acid is a colourless fuming liquid that turns tissue and tooth crowns yellow by making picric acid. Clothing stains yellow, gas distends the abdomen, and inhaled fumes injure the airway as well as the gut.
